title: Implement Rate Limiting for REST APIs
question: Design a rate limiting mechanism for your public REST API to prevent abuse. Requirements: 1) Limit requests per user/IP (100 requests per minute), 2) Return HTTP 429 Too Many Requests when limit exceeded, 3) Include rate limit headers (X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset), 4) Support different limits for different endpoints (public vs authenticated), 5) Distributed rate limiting across multiple servers. Use Spring interceptors, Redis for distributed counting, and Bucket4j/Resilience4j. Discuss: sliding window vs fixed window, handling burst traffic, rate limit per user vs per IP, and graceful degradation.
realWorldScenario: Protecting API from abuse with rate limits

title: Design Cursor-Based Pagination for Large Datasets
question: Your API returns a list of transactions (millions of records). Offset-based pagination performs poorly (OFFSET 1000000 is slow). Implement cursor-based pagination that: 1) Uses a cursor (encoded last seen ID + timestamp) instead of page numbers, 2) Returns next/previous cursor in response, 3) Handles deleted records gracefully, 4) Supports sorting by multiple fields, 5) Works efficiently with database indexes. Compare cursor vs offset pagination trade-offs. Discuss: cursor encoding/decoding, handling concurrent modifications, ensuring consistent ordering, and when to use cursor vs offset pagination.

title: Design Bulk Operations API for Batch Processing
question: Design a bulk operations API that allows clients to create/update/delete multiple resources in a single request. Requirements: 1) Accept array of operations in request body, 2) Process operations transactionally (all or nothing) or individually (partial success), 3) Return detailed results for each operation (success/failure with error messages), 4) Handle validation errors for individual items, 5) Limit batch size (max 1000 items). Use @Valid for validation, @Transactional for atomicity. Discuss: transactional vs non-transactional bulk ops, error handling strategies, rate limiting bulk requests, and idempotency concerns.
realWorldScenario: Efficient batch processing through REST API

title: Implement JWT-Based Authentication for REST APIs
question: Implement stateless authentication for your REST API using JWT tokens. Requirements: 1) Login endpoint returns JWT access token (15 min) and refresh token (7 days), 2) Protect endpoints with JWT validation, 3) Support token refresh without re-login, 4) Invalidate tokens on logout (blocklist), 5) Include user roles/permissions in token claims. Use Spring Security, JWT library (jjwt), and Redis for token blocklist. Discuss: token storage on client, token expiry strategy, refresh token rotation, preventing token theft (XSS/CSRF), and revoking tokens.

title: Implement HTTP Caching for REST APIs
question: Optimize your REST API performance with HTTP caching. Requirements: 1) Implement ETag-based caching (return 304 Not Modified if unchanged), 2) Add Cache-Control headers for cacheable responses, 3) Support conditional requests (If-None-Match, If-Modified-Since), 4) Invalidate cache on resource updates, 5) Handle versioned resources. Use Spring @Cacheable, ETag generation (MD5/SHA), and HTTP headers. Discuss: ETag vs Last-Modified, cache validation, cache busting strategies, CDN integration, and trade-offs between server-side vs client-side caching.
realWorldScenario: Reducing bandwidth and improving performance with caching

title: Build Comprehensive Request Validation Framework
question: Build a validation framework that validates incoming REST requests comprehensively. Requirements: 1) Field-level validation (required, format, range), 2) Cross-field validation (startDate < endDate), 3) Business rule validation (check if email already exists), 4) Return structured validation errors with field names, 5) Support internationalized error messages. Use @Valid, custom validators, @ControllerAdvice for error handling. Discuss: validation order (syntax → semantic → business), async validation for external checks (database), performance impact, and validation groups for different scenarios.
realWorldScenario: Robust input validation with detailed error messages

title: Generate Interactive API Documentation with OpenAPI
question: Generate comprehensive, interactive API documentation for your REST APIs. Requirements: 1) Auto-generate OpenAPI 3.0 spec from code annotations, 2) Provide Swagger UI for testing endpoints, 3) Document request/response schemas, status codes, examples, 4) Include authentication flows, 5) Keep documentation in sync with code. Use SpringDoc OpenAPI (springdoc-openapi-ui), annotations (@Operation, @ApiResponse), and customization. Discuss: annotation-based vs code-first vs API-first approach, versioning documentation, hosting options, and integrating with API gateways.

title: Implement Idempotency Keys for Payment APIs
question: Implement idempotency for payment processing API to prevent duplicate charges. Requirements: 1) Client sends Idempotency-Key header with each request, 2) Server stores request details with key for 24 hours, 3) Duplicate requests return cached response (same status, same result), 4) Handle concurrent requests with same key (lock and wait), 5) Clean up expired keys. Use Redis for idempotency key storage, distributed locks for concurrency. Discuss: key generation strategy (UUID), key expiration, handling partial failures (retry same key), and difference between idempotency and deduplication.

title: Design Webhook System for Event Notifications
question: Design a webhook system that notifies external systems about events (order created, payment completed). Requirements: 1) Clients register webhook URLs for specific events, 2) System sends HTTP POST with event data to registered URLs, 3) Retry failed deliveries with exponential backoff (max 5 attempts), 4) Provide webhook logs and delivery status, 5) Verify webhook authenticity (HMAC signature). Use async processing (@Async), retry mechanism, and queue (RabbitMQ/SQS) for reliability. Discuss: ordering guarantees, handling slow/down endpoints, rate limiting webhooks, security (signature verification), and webhook debugging.

title: Build API Gateway with Request Routing and Aggregation
question: Build an API Gateway that sits in front of 10 microservices. Requirements: 1) Route requests to appropriate microservice based on path, 2) Aggregate responses from multiple services into single response, 3) Handle authentication centrally (JWT validation), 4) Implement rate limiting and request logging, 5) Circuit breaker for failed services. Use Spring Cloud Gateway, Resilience4j, and load balancing. Discuss: gateway vs service mesh, request transformation, response caching, handling partial failures in aggregation, and performance overhead.
